description: Beam-width sweep (b=50,100,200,300) for LinearRaccess accuracy against the exact reference, on the 1,770 bpRNA sequences with 300<=length<=1000nt (the three longer length bins of Table 1). Supports Supplementary Information S3.
software_revision_note: New (beam_50/200/300) data embeds a dirty working-tree revision, violating software.lock.json's allow_dirty_worktree=false policy. The only uncommitted change present at generation time was the default -beam value edit later committed as bbba4549c776c51fa63c2cc1c571ea4e68faf2e6, and beam was passed explicitly on every invocation, so this is provenance noise rather than a computational difference; see software.lock.json's notes for the full account. reused_data below (exact_reference, beam_100) was generated cleanly at 892c93c8 (no -dirty suffix).

residual_failures_max_error_gt_0.5.note: Count of sequences (of 1,770) with at least one position/window absolute error exceeding 0.5. CORRECTED (independently re-verified 2026-09-16): this subset relationship does NOT hold at beam=50 -- 716 of its 1,380 failures are sequences that are fine at beam=100 (i.e. beam=50 is weaker than beam=100, so it fails on a different, larger population, not a strict subset of the 791). The subset relationship DOES hold at beam=200 (all 152 subset of the 791) and beam=300 (all 35 subset of the 791): no sequence newly crosses this threshold when the beam is increased ABOVE 100. Maximum observed error at beam=300 is 0.9129. The manuscript's own beam=300 claim (Supplementary S3) is scoped correctly to beam=300 only and is unaffected by this correction.
